text: Patient Ravi Kumar, 54 year old male. Chief complaint fever and body ache for 3 days. History of hypertension and type 2 diabetes.
Vitals: Blood pressure 150/95 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, temperature 101 F, weight 78 kg.
Prescription: Tab Dolo 650 mg (paracetamol) three times daily for 3 days. Tab Telmisartan 40 mg once daily.
Allergies: Penicillin allergy documented, rash and swelling. Avoid amoxicillin.
Lab report: HbA1c 8.2 percent, fasting blood glucose 162 mg/dL. Indicates poor glycemic control, diabetes mellitus.
Lipid profile: total cholesterol 220 mg/dL, LDL 140 mg/dL. Advised statin therapy, atorvastatin 10 mg.
Patient Meena Iyer, 41 year old female. Presented with migraine headache and nausea.
Prescription: Tab Crocin (acetaminophen) 500 mg as needed for pain. Sumatriptan 50 mg at onset of migraine.
Discharge summary: Appendectomy performed laparoscopically. Recovery uneventful. Follow up in 2 weeks.
Chest X-ray report: No pneumonia. Mild cardiomegaly noted. Lungs clear.
Allergies: Sulfa drug allergy. No known food allergies.
Patient John Mathew, 63 year old male. Admitted with myocardial infarction. ECG shows ST elevation.
Medications: Aspirin 75 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, metoprolol 25 mg. Blood pressure 130/85 mmHg.
Discharge advice: low salt diet, cardiac rehabilitation, follow up with cardiologist in 1 week.
